meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (International Companies regime administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority - SIFA)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - English common law tradition overlaid with customary law and a distinct offshore corporate statutory regime under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER) Plus - in force for Samoa since 2020
Samoa-New Zealand Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA)
China-Samoa framework cooperation under the Belt and Road Initiative (non-BIT investment facilitation instrument)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018 (Samoa); International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); United Nations Sanctions Act of Samoa and implementing UN Security Council sanctions regulations; SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for International Companies and Registered Agents; directives of the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access - the Register of Directors, Shareholders and Beneficial Owners is confidential, maintained at the licensed registered agent in Samoa, and disclosed to the Registrar, SIFA and the FIU only upon lawful demand; no public UBO register exists

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport for each director, shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC Notary Office and PRC Exit-Entry Administration with police-certified identity confirmation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain: PRC notarization, PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, Embassy of Samoa in Beijing final visa authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of Chinese business license (营业执照) and corporate certificate of incumbency (if any shareholder is a corporate entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain: PRC notarization, PRC MFA legalization, Embassy of Samoa in Beijing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank and professional reference letters confirming identity, reputation and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed PRC commercial bank and external legal counsel or certified public accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer signature notarized by PRC Notary Office, followed by PRC MFA legalization and Embassy of Samoa consular legalization; bank-to-agent direct verification acceptable at registered agent discretion

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the SIFA-licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant and each UBO executed before a PRC Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain: PRC notarization, PRC MFA legalization, Embassy of Samoa in Beijing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized criminal record certificate (无犯罪记录证明) for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC Ministry of Public Security / local public security bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization chain: PRC notarization, PRC MFA legalization, Embassy of Samoa in Beijing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Address or recent utility bill proving physical residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC utility company and local residential authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by PRC Notary Office, followed by PRC MFA legalization and Embassy of Samoa consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2018; mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, Samoa domestic sanctions designations, OFAC SDN List and FATF public statements; enhanced due diligence automatically triggered for politically exposed persons (PEPs) and family members, including senior PRC officials, with mandatory senior management approval of the registered agent and ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Registrar of International and Foreign Companies; name applications are filed exclusively through a SIFA-licensed registered agent, not via a public self-service portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Roman/Latin script; Chinese characters may be registered concurrently as a secondary dual name without statutory effect; all-Chinese articles of association are permissible provided a certified English summary or translation is retained by the registered agent; the name must not contain any token implying connection with a government or state organ
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registered agent shall lodge a written administrative reconsideration with the Registrar within 14 days, attaching prior-use evidence, consent letters or disclaimers; if the reconsideration is denied, an appeal may be filed with the responsible Minister and thereafter with the Supreme Court of Samoa under Part IV of the International Companies Act 1987; a fresh name application may be concurrently pre-screened by SIFA before formal filing to reduce rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office not permissible for the statutory registered office. The IC must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of the SIFA-licensed registered agent, where the registers of directors, members and beneficial owners are physically maintained. The commercial operations (study-abroad placement and immigration/visa advisory) may be conducted entirely remotely from the PRC without physical Samoan presence, provided the registered agent can produce statutory records on demand.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the IC itself (approximately 5% annual probability); moderate for the registered agent, which is subject to periodic AML/CFT and statutory-record inspections by SIFA and the FIU; unannounced physical inspections of the agent's Samoa premises are credible, and failure to produce UBO records on request can trigger immediate suspension of the IC.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Sections 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 18, 22 and 33 (incorporation, memorandum and articles, registered office, directors and secretary, share capital, and registered agent requirements)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Companies Registry Division under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company) and Form IC-2 (Consent and Particulars of Registered Agent and Registered Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; International Company may issue shares without par value; paid-up capital disclosed in the Memorandum; no escrow account requirement under the International Companies Act 1987; capital may be subscribed in any currency approved by the registered agent
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company adopt the Memorandum and Articles of Association as filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority. RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, and that the registered agent be authorized to receive service of process. RESOLVED that the subscriber shares be allotted and issued to the founding shareholder in accordance with the share subscription recorded in the Memorandum. RESOLVED that the following persons be and are hereby appointed as directors and secretary of the Company to hold office until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts, execute all incorporation filings, and take all steps necessary to obtain operating licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engage a Licensed Registered Agent and Reserve Company Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Companies Registry; licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a SIFA-licensed registered agent to conduct a name availability search and reserve the proposed International Company name. Submit a name reservation request with the proposed name clearly distinguishing the entity from any existing registered company and any name likely to mislead. The registered agent will file Form IC-R with the Companies Registry; after approval, the name will be reserved for a period of 30 days. Ensure the name includes a permitted suffix such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', or 'International Company' to denote limited liability.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Name Reservation (Form IC-R)
Proposed Company Name and Suffix
Identification documents of the founding shareholder (certified passport copy)
Due diligence questionnaire and reference letter from a bank or professional
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as indistinguishable or prohibited, submit a revised name immediately or file a written appeal with SIFA within 14 days of refusal, supported by a legal opinion distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting mark.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent and founding shareholder; notarized before a Samoa notary public or a notary in the jurisdiction of execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English (or accompanied by a certified English translation) incorporating the company name, registered office clause, share capital structure, objects clause, director and secretary provisions, and indemnity provisions. The Memorandum must be executed by the subscriber (founder) and witnessed in accordance with the International Companies Act 1987. If executed outside Samoa, the execution must be notarized and legalized or apostilled as required. Deliver the executed documents to the licensed registered agent for electronic or physical filing with SIFA.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent of Registered Agent (Form IC-2)
Consent of Subscriber / Founding Shareholder
Notarized signatures of each subscriber and witness
Certificate of Incumbency for the founding shareholder (where available)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries the memorandum or articles for non-compliance, the registered agent will revise the offending provisions and resubmit; any fee for resubmission is borne by the client, and curative amendments are executed by a director’s written consent in lieu of a meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Application for Incorporation with SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority, Companies Registry (online portal: SIFA e-Registry; physical counter: Apia head office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for incorporation by filing Form IC-1 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles, Form IC-2, and the prescribed filing fee of USD 250 (or equivalent in Samoan Tala). The registered agent will verify that the company name is reserved, that at least one director and one secretary are named, that the registered office is in Samoa, and that the share capital clause complies with the act. Upon successful vetting, SIFA will issue a Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number, date of incorporation, and the name of the International Company.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation)
Form IC-2 (Registered Agent and Registered Office Consent)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (executed)
Name Reservation Certificate
Certified identification documents of directors, secretary, and shareholder
Proof of filing fee payment (bank receipt or electronic payment confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, the registered agent will file a formal response or corrective amendment with SIFA within 7 business days; missing documents are supplemented, and any filing errors are corrected. A fresh application may be resubmitted without penalty if the defect is cured before certificate issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Directors, Secretary, and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority; directors and secretary appointed by the sole incorporator or by written resolution of the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon incorporation, the subscriber must hold a written resolution or first board resolution appointing the initial directors, the company secretary, and confirming the registered office at the licensed registered agent’s address in Apia. A minimum of one director is required; directors and secretary may be natural persons or corporate entities, and non-residents are permitted. File Form IC-3 / Notice of Directors and Secretary with SIFA within 30 days of any appointment or change. The registered office must be open during business hours and staffed by the registered agent.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution or Written Consent of Subscriber
Form IC-3 (Notice of Directors and Secretary)
Consent letters signed by each director and secretary
Certified identification and proof of address for each director and secretary
Registered Office Consent (Form IC-2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA does not accept the appointment forms, file a corrective notice and obtain written consents from the affected appointees; late filing penalties for director changes may be avoided by demonstrating excusable neglect and filing within 14 days of the query.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Account and Obtain Regulatory Endorsement for AML
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in Samoa (e.g., Samoa Commercial Bank, ANZ Samoa, Bank South Pacific) and the Samoa International Finance Authority AML/CFT Supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Certificate of Incorporation, the constitution/Memorandum and Articles, the directors' resolution on account opening and authorized signatories, and the due diligence package with the chosen commercial bank. The bank will conduct enhanced customer due diligence because the entity’s commercial model is immigration and study-abroad advisory, classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced under AML rules. For the International Company, the registered agent must also obtain an economic substance declaration or tax residency certificate if the company intends to claim treaty benefits or be considered managed from Samoa; otherwise file a declaration of non-residency with SIFA. No separate AML license is required for incorporation, but a business license under the Companies Act and the Business Licence Act 1998 (Samoa) may be required for operational activity.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Memorandum and Articles of Association
First Board Resolution and appointment of signatories
Certified passport copies of beneficial owner, directors and authorized signatories
Bank reference letter and source of funds declaration
AML/CFT questionnaire and business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional details, the company shall promptly provide a corporate profile, an organizational chart, and written clarifications. If an account is denied due to unresolved enhanced due diligence, the company may apply to another licensed bank or file an escalation with the SIFA AML supervisor to facilitate compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt First Board Resolution and Corporate Governance Minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; minutes registered in the company’s statutory records maintained by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors or obtain a written resolution signed by all directors. The pro-forma first board resolution must approve the issue of subscriber shares, confirm the registered office, and appoint the initial officers. Record the minutes in the statutory register, maintain a share register, directors' register, and charges register. Retention of corporate records in Samoa is required only as determined by SIFA guidelines; alternatively keep records at a location notified to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma First Board Resolution
Minutes of initial board meeting (or written consent)
Share register and register of directors/secretary
Register of charges (if any)
Statutory records binder maintained by registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If minutes or registers are incomplete, the board shall ratify them at the next meeting or by unanimous written resolution. Failure to maintain the registers is a compliance default and may be cured by retroactive completion and certification by the registered agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Samoa Business Licence and Taxpayer Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa Ministry of Revenue (formerly Samoa Revenue Corporation), and the Samoa Chamber of Commerce and Industry for business licence processing; tax office in Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Samoa Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and a Business Licence under the Business Licence Act 1998 before commencing operations. The application must describe the intended activities: international student placement, immigration and visa advisory services. Submit the Certificate of Incorporation, the first board resolution, a completed business licence application form (BL-1), proof of registered office, and payment of the licence fee. For an International Company that is tax-exempt on offshore income, an Exemption Certificate or a non-residence declaration must be issued by the Ministry of Revenue. The business licence must be renewed annually; the company should not engage in general domestic trading activity without converting to a Samoa Local Company for tax purposes.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Business Licence application form (BL-1)
Taxpayer Identification Number application
First Board Resolution for tax filing and business registration
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Description of intended activities and projected revenue
Proof of registered office and registered agent consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Licence application is denied or deferred, the Ministry of Revenue will state deficiency reasons; the applicant may file a revised application with a revised business scope or provide additional explanations. If the TIN is not issued within 14 days, the applicant may escalate to the Taxpayer Advocate Unit or submit a manual application to the Apia tax office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Business Licence Unit; Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) for International Company regulatory supervision
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence under the Business Licence Act 1998 (Samoa) with sectoral endorsement for Education and Training Services and Immigration/Visa Advisory Services; additional 'Agency for Foreign Student Placement' permit where applicable

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Pollution Control and Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment for an office-based advisory and consultancy service; registration under the MNRE Environmental Registry is required if the business generates waste streams or temporary construction; office operations fall under the 'Registration' category
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The business shall comply with the Water Resources Management Act 2008 and the Samoan National Building Code for waste disposal; no industrial wastewater or VOC emissions are expected; all municipal waste and electronic waste from office operations must be handled through licensed waste carriers; if any client meetings generate printed records, confidential paper waste shall be shredded and disposed via licensed recyclers; office generators or air-conditioning units, if installed, must meet Samoan noise and emissions thresholds for light-commercial use

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy Certificate and Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) for the Apia registered office; structural load inspection by the MCIL Building Inspectorate for a Class 1 or Class 2 commercial office space; occupational health and safety clearance for the workplace ensuring safe electrical wiring, emergency exits, and sanitation facilities; certificate of building compliance under the Samoa National Building Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MFR), Government of Samoa; MFR eServices taxpayer portal at https://www.mfr.gov.ws. The Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) administers incorporation, licensing, and annual government fees for International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 1987 (ICA 1987).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign beneficial owner must engage a SIFA-licensed registered agent (a Samoa trust or corporate management company) to incorporate the IC. The agent files the Memorandum and Articles of Association; SIFA issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a company registration number and annual fee schedule (minimum USD 200 for authorized capital up to USD 10,000; maximum USD 2,000). The agent then applies to MFR for a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) through the electronic Taxpayer Registration System (eTRS), submitting the Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent consent, beneficial ownership declaration, and foreign address of directors. The TIN is required for bank account opening, GST registration, and any customs transactions. Because the IC is exempt from income tax under ICA 1987 s.191 and does not derive Samoa-source assessable income, no corporate income tax registration is required beyond the TIN; however, a Foreign Investment Certificate under the Foreign Investment Act 2000 may be needed if the IC engages in any local or licensed activity in Samoa other than purely offshore advisory business. All filings with SIFA and MFR are transacted through the registered agent due to the non-resident nature of the directors and shareholders.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: A Samoa IC is a resident-incorporated limited company but is statutorily exempt from Samoa income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and estate duty on all income, assets, and transactions, provided it does not carry on business in Samoa with Samoa residents or own Samoa real property. The IC is not a pass-through entity for tax purposes; it is an entity-level exempt company. Its non-resident shareholders receive dividends free of Samoa withholding tax, and no branch profit tax applies. Foreign-source fees, including study-abroad placement commissions and immigration/golden-visa consultancy income earned exclusively from non-resident clients, fall within the offshore exemption zone and are subject to 0% taxation in Samoa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under the ICA 1987 and the Tax Administration Act 2012, the IC may: (1) elect in writing to be treated as a non-resident company for income tax purposes, reinforcing the offshore exemption; (2) apply to MFR for a binding tax ruling confirming the absence of a Samoa permanent establishment and the zero-rating of offshore services; (3) elect not to register for GST where all supplies are zero-rated exports and input credits are immaterial; and (4) elect to continue or redomicile to another jurisdiction under ICA 1987 s.230 as a defensive restructuring measure. Samoa has not enacted OECD hybrid-mismatch rules or a US-style check-the-box election; the general anti-avoidance provisions in the Tax Administration Act 2012 (ss.64-66) would disallow any arrangement whose sole purpose is to use the IC to defeat the tax law of a treaty or non-treaty jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Samoa Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, as amended; formerly VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (approximately USD 36,000) in annual taxable supplies over any rolling 12-month period, as prescribed in section 14 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1992; non-resident suppliers of remote/digital services to Samoa consumers are separately registrable under the cross-border services rules. A Samoa IC whose only supplies are zero-rated export services to non-residents may apply for exemption from GST registration; the registered agent should confirm the current threshold with MFR, as it is subject to ministerial adjustment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing mandate. GST-registered ICs must file quarterly GST returns electronically through MFR eServices by the last day of the month following each quarter. Tax invoices must contain the supplier's name and TIN, invoice number and date, description of the zero-rated or taxable supply, GST amount, and total consideration. For physical document shipments, customs data must be transmitted through the ASYCUDA World customs system; for pure service exports (study-abroad placement and visa advisory), no customs clearance is required and the contractual invoice package serves as the fiscal control record. MFR reserves the right to require e-invoicing data in CSV/PDF format upon audit demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An IC may claim 0% GST and income-tax exemption on fees derived from (1) the direct export of goods from Samoa; (2) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time the services are performed and who does not consume the services in Samoa; and (3) advisory services in the ISIC 7810 scope, namely international student placement and immigration/golden-visa consultancy, provided the IC has no Samoa-resident client, no Samoa office employees, and no local asset usage. The escrow-account and wire-transfer payment rails must evidence settlement by non-resident principals. Input VAT on local agent fees, legal fees, and bank charges is creditable against any output VAT; where zero-rated outputs exceed taxable outputs, the IC may claim a cash refund from MFR within 60 days of the quarterly return, subject to document verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SGD 1 form) for any physical document or package shipped outside Samoa
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement out of Samoa (if applicable)
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by a licensed Samoa commercial bank evidencing receipt of client fees from abroad
Executed service agreement and zero-rated tax invoices identifying the non-resident client, the offshore service description, and the stated ISIC 7810 activity
SIFA Certificate of Good Standing and MFR confirmation letter attesting the IC's tax-exempt status
Beneficial ownership statement and AML/KYC file for the escrow payment account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MFR conducts desk and field audits of zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate the offshore nature of services within the 180-day repatriation window triggers retrospective clawback of all GST refunds plus statutory late-payment interest (approximately 10% per annum). Fraudulent or reckless claims attract shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012: 20% base penalty for mere error, 75% for gross negligence, and 150% for intentional evasion, alongside criminal prosecution of the directors and the registered agent with fines up to WST 100,000 and imprisonment up to five years for falsifying export documents. The Central Bank of Samoa may additionally impose exchange-control penalties for unrepatriated export earnings, and SIFA may strike off the IC and revoke the registered agent's license where the IC is used to facilitate fraudulent visa or tax avoidance schemes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), Exchange Control Department, acting under the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations 1984, and the Financial Institutions Act 1996.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed-float regime pegged to an undisclosed weighted basket of partner currencies dominated by NZD, AUD, and USD. Current-account transactions for trade in services, including education, study-abroad placement, and immigration advisory fees, are freely convertible through authorized dealer banks without central bank pre-approval. Capital-account movements, including foreign-currency borrowing by Samoan residents, require Exchange Control approval. An International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is statutorily treated as non-resident for exchange-control purposes: it may maintain foreign-currency deposits with authorized dealers, freely remit dividends, advisory fees, and liquidation proceeds abroad, and operate without converting receipts into WST. Profit and capital remittance from a Samoan IC to non-resident shareholders or ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) is not subject to Samoan withholding tax, provided the IC's income-tax exemption certificate remains valid and the bank receives standard evidential filings: certificate of good standing, board resolution authorizing the payment, and, for dividend distributions, a directors' solvency declaration registered with the Registrar of International Companies. Residual practical impediments arise only from the correspondent-bank compliance layer of the receiving bank jurisdiction, not from Samoan exchange-control measures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For Samoan resident trading entities, the Exchange Control Regulations 1984 and CBS practice require foreign-currency export proceeds to be declared, repatriated through an authorized dealer, and either credited to a CBS-approved foreign-currency account or converted into WST, with the standard export declaration form referencing a 30-day realization timeline from shipment. A mandatory 100% conversion ratio applies only where proceeds are brought into WST as a matter of CBS direction, not as an automatic rule. International Companies are outside the resident exchange-control net: no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply to an IC's foreign-currency receipts. For the ISIC 7810 study-abroad and immigration-visa consultancy scope, the 'export' consists of cross-border professional services; such fees may be credited directly to the IC's foreign-currency account at an authorized dealer without conversion to WST. WST conversion is undertaken only to fund specific local operating liabilities in Samoa, and the IC should maintain a dual-currency structure to avoid unnecessary bid-offer spreads.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules_addendum: For the avoidance of doubt, the IC shall file no CBS export declaration for service receipts, but must retain underlying client contracts, invoices, and evidence of service delivery in the treasury file to respond to any authorized-dealer audit inquiry, because Samoan banks still classify the IC as a monitored non-resident commercial account for anti-money-laundering purposes.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in multi-currency (USD/WST/NZD) plus designated sub-account for client-fee segregation (escrow-style bookkeeping)
Foreign-Currency Deposit Account and WST Operational Current Account
Operational Account and dedicated Client Trust / Escrow Account for immigration-application deposits

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a primary treasury rail. Samoa has no electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime; the Financial Institutions Act 1996 restricts deposit-taking and money-transmission activities to licensed banks and licensed money-changers, preventing any offshore digital EMI (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) from legally operating a Samoa-domiciled settlement account or sponsoring a Samoan IC as a direct participant. Offshore EMIs may be used only as an ancillary inbound collection channel for client fees from foreign jurisdictions, with the IC thereafter executing a weekly consolidation sweep to its BSP Samoan account. Legal constraints include: (i) EMI client funds held in a foreign pooled account are not client-money protected under Samoan law; (ii) Samoan licensed banks will reject outbound instructions sourced from an unlicensed EMI due to liability and sanctions-screening concerns; and (iii) the IC's own AML/CFT obligations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 require look-through evidence of the underlying payor, which foreign EMIs often do not provide at the required granularity. Recommended architecture: BSP Samoa as the master treasury account; a licensed New Zealand or Australian bank as the collection and disbursement hub for the global Chinese/other client base; and an offshore EMI only for low-value, non-recurring receipt niches not exceeding 20% of aggregate monthly receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is not statutorily required for a Samoan IC account opening. In practice, BSP and SCB permit remote onboarding of non-resident directors subject to: (i) introduction by the IC's licensed Samoan registered agent (licensed under the International Companies Act 1987 by the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour); (ii) notarized copies of the directors' passports and proof-of-residence, apostilled or legalized as required; and (iii) a live video-identification interview with the bank's compliance officer, arranged through the registered agent. UBOs with a 25% or greater beneficial interest must be identified and may be required to appear in the video interview if the account signatory is a nominee director. A local in-person signature is required from the registered agent's authorised representative (a Samoa-resident director or corporate secretary) on the account mandate at the date of opening. The IC must register a compliance address in Samoa, which is the registered agent's office; no physical trading address is required. For the medium-risk ISIC 7810 classification, banks apply enhanced due diligence, and the final sign-off is typically conditional on receipt of the IC's business plan, projected transaction volumes, and destination-country licensing evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source-of-funds pattern: the IC receives lump-sum client fees for study-abroad and golden-visa placement, creating unexplained-wealth or third-party-payment red flags for the bank's suspicious-transaction reporting unit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) executed client services agreements with fee schedules for each engagement; (ii) simplified invoice register with source-of-funds declaration from each client; (iii) university offer letters or immigration-application lodgement receipts as transactional evidence; (iv) the IC's overseas collection-account statements; and (v) a board-approved AML/CFT compliance manual tailored to the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and the Financial Intelligence Unit's guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remittance clustering from high-risk corridors or frequent involvement of politically exposed persons (PEPs) in golden-visa applications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain (i) enhanced due diligence (EDD) files on PEP-adjacent clients containing wealth-origin attestations; (ii) a jurisdiction risk-scoring matrix covering all client nationalities; (iii) sanctions-screening screenshots for every instructing party and beneficiary, referencing UN, OFAC, EU, and Samoan FIU lists; and (iv) an independent AML audit report on the IC's transaction-monitoring system issued within the preceding 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin and evidently opaque capital structure: the IC has no minimum capital requirement, yet routes large six-figure tuition and disbursement flows, creating an inference of round-tripping or unauthorized money services business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce (i) a certified sources-and-uses cash-flow projection; (ii) a declaration that funding comprises shareholder loans and prepaid client funds, with notarized loan agreements at arm's-length interest; (iii) accrual-basis financial statements prepared by a licensed Samoan accountant; and (iv) a written and visually documented description of the operational segregation between the IC's own funds and the client-fee escrow sub-ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory-status gaps: banks may question whether the IC holds an immigration-service license in its operating markets, because unlicensed migration assistance is a prohibited activity in most source countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File (i) the Samoan business license and the IC's certificate of incorporation; (ii) for outbound services to major markets, destination-country authorizations, such as Australian MARA immigration-agent registration, New Zealand immigration-adviser licensing, or the relevant Canadian/UK regulatory enrollment; and (iii) a signed undertaking that the IC will only handle clients for whom the relevant authorization or a permitted referral arrangement exists, with mandatory refund provisions mirrored in the client terms.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are executed as SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the shareholder's bank to the IC's foreign-currency account at BSP Samoa, using remittance information field 70 identifying 'CAPT' (capital contribution / share subscription) under the ISO 20022 or SWIFT purpose conventions. The receiving bank requires the following verification pack: (i) board resolution authorizing the share issue and identifying the bank account; (ii) updated register of members evidencing the subscribing shareholder; (iii) beneficial-ownership declaration for the UBO; and (iv) source-of-wealth summary for the shareholder, notarized in the jurisdiction of origin. For funds destined to be used as intercompany working capital rather than share capital, the routing is identical but purpose-field 'SLOA' (shareholder loan) must be displayed, and an executed loan agreement with a commercial interest rate must be pre-filed to avoid transfer-pricing or thin-capitalization challenge in the shareholder's home jurisdiction. No central-bank prior approval is required for foreign-currency capital injections into a non-resident IC, but the bank's internal EDD committee may impose a 3–5 business-day hold pending verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements comprise two principal rails. Rail 1 - institutional tuition and program-placement payments: SWIFT MT103 from the BSP foreign-currency account to the beneficiary university's bank, with purpose code '2310' or 'EDUCATION' as recognized by the clearing network, beneficiary full legal name, address, and the student's application reference; a commercial letter of credit is economically unsuitable for recurring tuition payments and is not recommended. Rail 2 - government and embassy visa-fee payments: direct SWIFT MT103 to the official fee-collection accounts of the relevant immigration authority or authorized embassy, with the application number in the payment narrative to ensure correct allocation. For local Samoan operating expenses in WST, settlement runs through the domestic clearing network operated by the Central Bank of Samoa, subject to CBS transaction-reporting thresholds. The IC shall maintain a payment-operations matrix containing each beneficiary's account details, expected clearing time, and contract reference, and shall set bank-client advisories to reject any instruction mismatching the pre-registered beneficiary to reduce fraud and compliance friction. SWIFT MT202 (bank-to-bank) is used only for cover payments where the receiving bank is not a direct participant; all commercial instructions must articulate underlying trade/service invoices.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla spot and forward foreign-exchange contracts with BSP Samoa or an offshore authorized dealer (NZD/USD crosses, WST/USD and WST/NZD tenors up to 12 months), permissible only against documented service-fee and operating-cost exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST executed with licensed offshore banks where the IC substantiates genuine economic exposure to WST conversion for local payroll and office costs
Cross-currency swaps (WST/USD or WST/AUD) with authorized dealer banks, subject to CBS market-volume limits and a signed ISDA/CSA or bank master agreement evidencing underlying hedging intent

Over-the-counter (OTC) currency options in G10 currencies (USD, NZD, AUD, EUR) to cap upside on client-fee collection corridors, available exclusively through bank treasury desks with a board-approved derivatives-usage policy

Exchange-traded currency futures in USD/NZD and USD/AUD via international brokerage, layered as a risk-mitigation overlay where the bank's credit line is limited; use of any WST cross on exchange-traded markets is unavailable and therefore impermissible
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.liquidity_concentration_and_stress_guida: The IC shall maintain a three-tier liquidity buffer: (i) Tier-1 operating liquidity equal to 90 days of average operating costs held in the BSP operational account; (ii) Tier-2 client-fee segregation sub-account held as a dedicated ledger balance and never commingled with operating funds; and (iii) Tier-3 reserves in a high-grade money-market fund domiciled in New Zealand or Australia. Withdrawal permissions and dual-approval thresholds shall be embedded in the bank signature cards: single-signature up to 10,000 WST equivalent; dual signatures above 10,000 WST equivalent; and the registered agent's counter-signature above 100,000 WST equivalent. All treasury transactions shall be reportable monthly to the board, with a quarterly reconciliation of purpose codes and underlying contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation Statement and Government Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the incorporation anniversary date; the Registrar may allow a short administrative grace period but no statutory extension is automatic
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee plus administrative charges; non-payment for 90 days beyond the anniversary triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution of the International Company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Compliance Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent for retention and onward submission to the Registrar of International Companies if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual renewal date (incorporation anniversary), or within 14 days of any relevant shareholding or beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit is a breach of the International Companies Act and AML/CFT obligations, subject to fines up to USD 1,000 and potential administrative strike-off if Persistent non-compliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None for a standard exempted International Company; a mandatory audit is triggered only if the company elects to be registered as a public international company or if the Registrar or shareholders require audited accounts under the company's articles
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No mandatory statutory accounting framework for International Companies; internal records may be maintained under IFRS, US GAAP, or any other reasonable accounting basis consistently applied

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a register of beneficial owners at its registered office and update it within 14 days of any change. No separate annual UBO filing is made to the Registrar for standard companies; however, the directors must provide the Registered Agent with a written annual confirmation verifying all shareholders and beneficial owners for AML/CFT purposes, with particular scrutiny of share transfers during the year

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 750 - USD 1,200 (standard discretionary annual Registered Agent fee)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - not required for standard International Companies; voluntary review or opinion: USD 400 - USD 800

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for an International Company (IC) on income derived from business conducted wholly outside Samoa under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 223; 25% standard corporate income tax (CIT) rate under the Income Tax Act 2015 for any resident company deriving income from a Samoan source.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies enjoy a de facto 0% effective tax rate on foreign-sourced revenue from study-abroad placement and immigration/golden-visa advisory fees. Statutory exemptions include: income tax exemption on offshore business income, exemption from value added goods and services tax (VAGST) on offshore supplies, exemption from stamp duty applicable to domestic instruments, and no capital gains tax. The IC regime substitutes income tax with a flat annual government fee payable to the Registrar of International Companies through the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) and the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Form IRD-CIT), filed electronically through the Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MfR) Online Taxpayer Services e-Filing portal; International Companies additionally file an International Company Annual Return and an Economic Substance Declaration with SIFA/MCIL through the corporate registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return for all companies; quarterly provisional tax instalments for companies with taxable Samoan-source income; monthly VAGST returns where registered. Exempt International Companies generally file a nil/administrative annual return and do not make provisional payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 March for a 31 December balance date; the Commissioner for Inland Revenue may grant an extension on written application before the due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoa TIN of the taxpayer entity as registered with the Ministry for Revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the IC TIN; verify that the TIN remains active and aligned with the SIFA/MCIL registration certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Entity Name and Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the company and the name of the licensed registered agent in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact name as it appears in the International Companies Act registration; confirm the registered agent holds a current SIFA license.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Tax Year and Basis Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax year (usually the calendar year) and the period of account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State 1 January to 31 December of the relevant year unless the Commissioner approved a substituted accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income derived from all business activities before deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an exempt IC, do not include foreign-sourced consultancy fees from study-abroad placement and visa advisory; these are statutorily exempt. Include any Samoan-source income, which would jeopardize IC status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Exempt Income and IC Register Reference
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income claimed as exempt, including offshore income of an International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule identifying the IC Act exemption (s. 223), the IBC/IC registration number, and evidence that management and control were exercised outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses incurred in producing assessable income, subject to the anti-avoidance rules of the Income Tax Act 2015.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No operating deductions are required if all income is exempt; nevertheless maintain transfer pricing documentation for inter-company fees (e.g., commissions to Chinese marketing affiliates).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Taxable Income and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income less allowable deductions, multiplied by the applicable CIT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 for an IC whose income is wholly foreign-sourced; enter 25% CIT for any inadvertently derived Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Withholding Tax Credits and Balance Due/Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for final withholding tax, provisional tax paid, and any refund or balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An exempt IC will disclose no credits and no balance due; file the return regardless to maintain good standing and obtain a tax clearance certificate for banking and repatriation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a default penalty based on the tax assessed (up to 10% of the net CIT), plus a compounding late payment surcharge of 2% per month of tax remaining unpaid; false or misleading statements attract a shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax avoided; the MfR may add collection costs and apply for a travel ban or asset freezing order against recalcitrant taxpayers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% final withholding tax on dividends or distributions paid by an International Company out of exempt offshore profits; 15% final withholding tax (FWT) under the Income Tax Act 2015 on dividends paid by a resident Samoan company to a non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority (e.g., the State Taxation Administration of China for PRC residents) and submit it, together with a completed MfR Treaty Relief Declaration/Form TR-1 and a beneficial ownership declaration, to the Samoan payer before the dividend is distributed. The payer must retain the TRC and declaration for at least five years. Under the Samoa-China DTA, dividends are capped at 5% where the beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the capital and 10% in all other cases, subject to MfR approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory FWT rates for non-residents are 15% for interest and 15% for royalties under the Income Tax Act 2015; under the Samoa-China DTA the rates are generally reduced to 10% for interest and 10% for royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and meets the treaty limitation-of-benefits conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No fixed statutory threshold in Samoan Tala (WST) is legislated for mandatory Local File or Master File preparation. The Commissioner for Inland Revenue may demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for any cross-border related-party transaction without a de minimis threshold. For an ISIC 7810 study-abroad and immigration-visa consultancy, any management fee, commission, or referral fee paid to a Chinese or Hong Kong affiliate should be documented as a matter of practice where the annual value of related-party transactions exceeds WST 500,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019 and the SIFA Economic Substance Guidance apply to International Companies engaged in relevant activities. The IC must be managed and controlled in Samoa, maintain adequate physical premises and qualified employees in Samoa, and incur proportionate local expenditure. For a study-abroad and immigration-visa advisory entity, the relevant activity is typically characterized as a 'distribution and service centre' or 'service business' where services are rendered to foreign related parties; where the IC only serves unrelated offshore clients, it must nonetheless file an Economic Substance Declaration and demonstrate genuine presence, or retain its IC tax exemption under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 223.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately booking Chinese student-placement fees, university commission rebates, and golden-visa success fees as exempt IC offshore income while management and control of the business are in fact exercised from Samoa or through a sham Hong Kong intermediary; failing to declare Samoan-source advisory fees in a resident company's income tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of hidden income at the 25% CIT rate; shortfall penalty of up to 150% of the tax evaded; compounding late payment interest at 2% per month; deregistration of the International Company and loss of the s. 223 exemption; criminal prosecution for tax evasion carrying fines and custodial terms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors risk personal liability where the corporate form is a mere facade; courts may pierce the corporate veil to collect unpaid tax and penalties; directors convicted of tax evasion face imprisonment and travel bans imposed by the Samoan courts at the MfR's request.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no registered office substance in Samoa, no local employees, no Samoan management meetings, and no SIFA Economic Substance Declaration, while using the entity solely as a pass-through collection vehicle for foreign client visa and tuition wire transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2019; strike-off and deregistration by the Registrar; revocation of the IC tax exemption with retroactive taxation at 25% CIT, including compensatory interest and penalties; exclusion from the international financial centre register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee and executive directors may be disqualified from holding office in licensed Samoan entities, fined personally, and held civilly liable for the resulting tax liabilities; the SIFA registrar may issue removal orders and referral to the Attorney General for criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating escrow accounts and receiving wire transfers from PRC-based clients for study-abroad and immigration visa products without conducting customer due diligence, verifying source of funds, or filing suspicious transaction reports; allowing the IC bank account to be used to move third-party funds for golden-visa applications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018: corporate fines up to WST 1,000,000 per offence; natural persons subject to fines and imprisonment of up to 14 years; forfeiture of funds; revocation of the IC's banking and SIFA licensing privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and nominated officers are personally prosecutable for AML failures; personal asset freezing and confiscation orders may be issued; convicted directors face imprisonment and prohibition from managing or controlling any financial or corporate service business in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Immigration Advisory and Ultra Vires Domestic Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting immigration/visa advisory and student placement services under an International Company license without holding the mandatory statutory license required for ISIC 7810 activity in Samoa, or selling such services to Samoan-resident individuals, thereby carrying on domestic business prohibited by the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Licensing penalties and consumer-protection sanctions; cancellation of the IC registration; the fees derived from prohibited onshore activity treated as Samoan-source income and taxed at 25% CIT plus penalties; the Registrar may refuse reinstatement and publicize the violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized unlicensed domestic advisory activity face fines and prosecution for acting without a required license; civil restitution to affected clients may be ordered; international immigration authorities may impose adverse travel and visa consequences on directors engaged in fraudulent immigration advisory practices.
